inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average for Q2 FY2026 (13 weeks to 2026-08-01, 10-Q filed 2026-08-28) = 456.6M; basic outstanding 454.3M at 2026-08-01. Held FLAT because SBC (plus equity-award withholding) is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $282M + taxes paid on net-share settlement $67M (no combined company figure published, so the two lines are summed). H1 FY2026 run-rate is higher ($154M + $92M), hence the 0.35% forward path.
inputs.fy0: FY2025 (fiscal year ended 2026-01-31; labelled FY2026 in Metrics.csv)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (A-rated) -> ~3.8% after tax; debt incl. finance and operating leases ~$19.2B vs ~$71.5B market cap (~21% debt weight) -> WACC ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged through the probability-weighted scenarios, not a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost (~$691M FY2025) is straight-line rent inside SG&A/COGS, so it is already inside EBITDA and the flows; operating-lease liabilities ($3.3B non-current) are therefore NOT in net debt. Finance-lease liabilities (~$2.1B) are inside LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations and their amortisation is inside D&A, so they sit in total_debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None - Target has no material non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (US operating retailer; routing table row 1/2 - consumer, moderately cyclical). No prior TGT DCF and no MEMORY entry: fresh build. ANCHORS: net debt = $14,221M long-term debt and finance leases + $1,136M current portion - $5,411M cash at 2026-08-01 (Q2 FY2026 10-Q via SEC XBRL companyfacts; cash is mid-year and seasonally low-to-mid vs the January peak). FY0 EBITDA margin: GAAP EBITDA $8,251M (op income 5,117 + D&A 3,134) + SBC 282 = $8,533M = 8.1% of revenue, but FY2025 Q1 carried ~$593M of one-off interchange-litigation settlement gains, so the underlying pre-SBC margin was ~7.6%. TARIFF REFUND: the $994M pretax IEEPA tariff refund recognised in Q2 FY2026 is EXCLUDED from every projected margin (Y1 base 8.3% = guided ~6% op margin less the ~90bp refund, + D&A ~3.0%, + SBC). It is not added to the bridge either: whatever has been collected is already inside the 2026-08-01 cash; any uncollected receivable (~$755M after tax, ~$1.65/share) is unmodelled upside. WORKING CAPITAL: inventory $13.2B ~ payables $13.3B at 2026-08-01, so growth is close to cash-neutral; wc_capture 0 (bear -2). BUYBACKS: $408M FY2025, ~$3M H1 FY2026 - repurchases effectively paused while capex steps up to ~$5B, so the flat count is a modelling convention Target is currently funding only partly. Interest income not stripped: Target is net debt. Horizon 10 years because capex (~4.5% of revenue in FY2026) is well above its mature ~3.4-3.6% and the margin is still recovering in year 5. Engine discounts year 1 as a full year from the valuation date although H1 FY2026 is already complete - a small conservative approximation. Fiscal-year labels in Metrics.csv run one year ahead of Target's own naming (CSV FY2026 = Target fiscal 2025), and the XBRL quarter rows for FY2026 are labelled 'Q2 2027'/'Q3 2027' (= Target Q1/Q2 2026).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (12.9%) diverges >30% from revenue 3yr (-1.3%): book value rebuilt from the FY2022 trough because buybacks were halted (FY2023 $0) and only partly resumed, not because the business grew. Equity 5yr (2.3%) is the conservative check and agrees with revenue 5yr, which is selected.
historical_growth.notes: Periods are Target fiscal years (CSV labels one year ahead). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes: FY2020 ~$7,666M (pandemic peak), FY2022 -$1,914M (inventory glut + $5.5B capex, so 3yr CAGR undefined), FY2023 $3,433M, FY2024 $4,070M, FY2025 $2,486M. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (-20.2%) is below reported (-18.5%) because SBC+withholding has risen from ~$210M to ~$349M while FCF fell; both start at a COVID-windfall base and say more about FY2020 than about the trend. EPS 3yr CAGR runs off the FY2022 inventory-markdown trough.

base.rationale: Y1 growth = FY2026 guidance (~5%; H1 already +6.0%). Margin recovers from the ~7.6% underlying FY2025 to 9.0% pre-SBC (~5.6% operating), below the 6%+ operating margin of FY2018-19 because Walmart/Costco/Amazon price pressure caps it. Capex steps down from the ~$5B FY2026 programme to 3.4% (still above D&A, funding ~30 stores/yr). Cash tax ~23% (FY2025 paid $1,091M).

bull.rationale: Turnaround works: comps stay +3-4%, new stores add ~1pt, Roundel and Circle 360 lift the mix so the pre-SBC margin returns to ~9.8% (~6.4% operating, the FY2018-19 level). Heavier capex sustained for the 300-store decade plan.

bear.rationale: H2 FY2026 fades once the tariff-refund and easy boycott comparisons lapse; grocery trips keep migrating to Walmart/Costco/Amazon, discretionary demand softens, and the margin stays in the FY2023-25 underlying range (~7.6-7.8% pre-SBC, ~4.3% operating). Capex cut back toward maintenance.

scenario_narratives.base: Fiddelke's plan delivers the guided ~5% FY2026 sales growth (H1 +6%, Q2 comp +3.8% with traffic +3.6%), then growth settles at ~3% as the boycott comparisons lapse: low-single-digit comps plus ~1pt from 30+ new stores a year. Roundel and Target Circle 360 add high-margin other revenue, and the operating margin climbs back to ~5.6% (pre-SBC EBITDA 9.0%) - better than the FY2023-25 ~5% underlying but short of the FY2018-19 6%+, because Walmart and Costco keep the price gap (~5% above Walmart) from narrowing on Target's terms. The $994M tariff refund is treated as a one-off and is in no forward year. The ~$5B capex year is a step, not a new run-rate: capex glides to 3.4% of sales.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Enterprise Acceleration Office turns the reset into sustained share gains: traffic stays positive, owned brands and the Home/Baby/seasonal refresh restore 'Tar-zhay' discovery, Roundel doubles as management targets and Circle 360 membership compounds, lifting mix. Sales grow 6% in FY2026 and 3.5-4% for several years as the 300-store decade plan executes; the operating margin returns to ~6.4%, matching FY2018-19, and the business earns a slightly higher exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026 recovery proves to be easy comparisons plus a tariff windfall. Grocery and essentials trips continue to migrate to Walmart (20-27% grocery share), Costco and Amazon/Whole Foods; Target's discretionary-heavy mix (apparel, home, electronics) meets a softer middle-income consumer and renewed tariff costs; reputational exposure from both sides of the DEI fight flares again. Sales grow ~1-2% after FY2026, the margin stays at the FY2023-25 underlying level, and the heavy capex programme earns little - management cuts it back. Investment-grade balance sheet means this is a value bear, not a solvency bear.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because the turnaround rests on a new CEO's unproven plan and two quarters of recovery against boycott-depressed comparisons. Base held at 50%: guidance and H1 actuals support it. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs comps, margin mix (Roundel/Circle 360) and store-growth returns to all go right at once against Walmart and Costco.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A mature US mass-merchant valued on owner FCF with the FY2026 tariff refund and the FY2025 litigation gain stripped from the margin base. The question the price asks is whether Target's operating margin returns to its pre-COVID ~6%: the base case assumes most, not all, of the way back.
key_risks_to_valuation: Operating-margin path: each 50bp of mature pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly $10/share
Grocery/essentials share loss to Walmart, Costco and Amazon reducing trip frequency
Tariff policy: the FY2026 refund shows how large tariff swings are relative to a ~5% operating margin
Return on the ~$5B capex step-up (new stores, 130+ remodels) - capex is held above D&A for a decade in every case
Brand/political exposure (2025 DEI boycott) and CEO-transition execution
Discretionary-heavy category mix in a consumer slowdown
